name: crea_records
description: One row per activity the AI moderation assistant evaluated. It becomes the participant history read back into the next evaluation, and the study data. Pseudonymous by design: the community is readable, the person is a pseudonym, the name is nowhere.

columns.name: record_uuid
columns.description: The identifier the record is known by outside this database. Unique.

columns.name: contribution_ref
columns.description: Which contribution this is about, as a reference rather than a foreign key — the record outlives the row it describes.

columns.name: person_pseudonym
columns.description: Stands in for the member. Never a user id and never a name — that is what makes the table shareable as study data.

columns.name: activity
columns.description: What was done, in the member's own words, shortened.

columns.name: category_key
columns.description: The taxonomy entry the activity was sorted into. Meaning depends on taxonomy_version.

columns.name: hours
columns.open: The type vocabulary has no floating point entry, on purpose — nothing else in the schema needs one. Hours could be an integer count of minutes and the question goes away. Decide before the Crea domain is rebuilt.

columns.name: hours_estimated
columns.description: Whether the assistant estimated the hours or the member stated them.

columns.name: crea_verdict
columns.open: An open string set in legacy. Contract it as an enum once the Crea domain is rebuilt — the same question events.type raises.

columns.name: applied_rule
columns.description: Which rule of ruleset_version produced the verdict.

columns.name: discrepancy
columns.description: Where the assistant and the moderator disagreed.

columns.name: moderator_final
columns.description: What the moderator decided in the end. NULL while nobody has looked.

columns.name: raw_text
columns.description: The submitted text as it was.
columns.note: This is the one column that can carry something identifying, since a member may name themselves in their own text. It is not study data in the sense the rest of the row is.

columns.name: model
columns.description: Which model produced the evaluation. NULL for a row written before the setting existed.

notes: The three version columns are what makes an old row readable: category_key, applied_rule and the verdicts only mean something together with the taxonomy, ruleset and behavior they were produced under. Re-interpreting an old row under today's taxonomy is wrong, and both implementations must carry the version through rather than dropping it.

No foreign keys, by the convention this table set and the creation-group join tables followed — see the open question in contribution_creation_groups.json. Here it is deliberate: contribution_ref survives the contribution being deleted.
person_pseudonym is the whole privacy design. An implementation that writes a user id, an alias or a name into it has not broken a column, it has broken the promise the table is built on.
Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json. This table uses datetime(3).
